name: Video frame sampling rate is the primary cost knob
symptom: Video inference cost is dominated by the frame sampling rate. A 1-minute video at 1 fps = 60 frames, but at 2 fps = 120 frames, doubling the cost.
root_cause: Each frame is processed independently by the vision encoder, so the total cost scales linearly with the number of frames. The frame sampling rate is the primary cost knob.
workaround: Reduce the frame sampling rate. For most applications, 0.5-1 fps is sufficient. Use keyframe sampling to only process frames with significant visual change. Use temporal pooling to pool adjacent frames before the LLM.
notes: FRAME SAMPLING IS THE PRIMARY COST KNOB FOR VIDEO: The total cost of video inference is frame_sampling_rate * tokens_per_frame * num_frames. For a 1-minute video at 1 fps = 60 frames, at 448x448 per frame with 2x2 spatial merge = 256 tokens per frame, total visual tokens = 60*256 = 15,360. At 2 fps, this doubles to 30,720 tokens. The frame sampling rate is the most important cost knob because it directly multiplies the per-frame cost. LLaVA-NeXT-Video uses 1 fps sampling. Pixtral uses variable frame sampling based on video duration. The token counts are derived from the model configs; the cost formula is standard.
